subject: Clarify bulk-license metering, proration and fallback plan for Acme Analytics listing
messages:
From: alex.jenkins@amazon.com <aws_marketplace_pm@amazon.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0000
Subject: Request: Clarify bulk-license metering & proration for Acme Analytics SaaS listing

Hi Logan / Marcus,

Working on the Acme Analytics listing preflight and have a few open questions on how Redwood plans to report bulk-license consumption (seat bundles + on-demand overage) and how proration should be reflected in the metering events. AWS Marketplace wants a short, documented fallback behavior if we can’t emit fine-grained per-seat events (e.g., during transient platform outages).

Specifically: 
- How will entitlements be represented for a bundle of 50 seats purchased as a single SKU? Will you emit one monthly aggregate unit or 50 unit events tied to a customer entitlement ID?
- If a subscription is prorated mid-billing-cycle (customer upgrades from 50 to 75 seats), do you plan to emit a separate proration event or send an adjusted cumulative usage report?
- What’s the graceful fallback if Redwood’s KV cache is temporarily unavailable (we need a recommended replay/backfill approach so AWS can reconcile usage with the entitlement mapping)?

Can you share a brief plan + attachments by EOD (US) so procurement at Acme can proceed with contract signature? We’d like a short note to include in the listing docs.

Thanks,
Alex Jenkins
Product Manager, AWS Marketplace
alex.jenkins@amazon.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: alex.jenkins@amazon.com, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify bulk-license metering & proration for Acme Analytics SaaS listing

Alex — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I attached an entitlement-matrix.csv to show how we plan to map SKUs -> entitlement IDs. Quick summary: 

- Bundle representation: We will emit per-seat events (one event per seat) when the customer requests per-seat reporting. For customers who opt for a single-aggregate SKU we will emit an aggregate monthly usage event tied to the purchase SKU. The entitlement-matrix.csv maps which accounts get per-seat vs aggregate.

- Proration approach: We emit a proration delta event at upgrade time (timestamped) with the delta units and a note linking to the effective_date. We also emit the cumulative usage at the end of the billing window. This gives Marketplace both the fine-grained change and a reconciliation anchor.

- Fallback & backfill: Primary behavior is prefix/KV caching + durable event log to S3. If the KV cache is unavailable we fall back to aggregate events at the end of the billing cycle and run a backfill job that replays tokenized events against the entitlement mapping. The backfill produces a reconciliation report (json) we will upload to the Drive link below and push a notification to AWS via the fulfillment webhook. See attached CSV for mapping examples.

I’m looping in Soojin for implementation details and a diagram of the fallback flow. Marcus — can you confirm SLA we should commit to for replay latency? Procurement at Acme wants to see 48–72 hour maximum for full reconciliation.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Sr. Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai

Attachment: entitlement-matrix.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: alex.jenkins@amazon.com, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify bulk-license metering & proration for Acme Analytics SaaS listing

Logan / Alex — adding the technical plan and the fallback diagram. Summary of the implementation plan: 

1) Entitlement modeling: Each purchase creates an entitlement object with fields {entitlement_id, sku_id, account_id, units_allocated, reporting_mode}. reporting_mode = [per-seat, aggregate]. This is materialized in our config DB and exported to S3 as a single mapping file every hour.

2) Metering events: For per-seat: we emit individual usage events with incremental counters. For aggregate: emit a single usage measurement per billing window (or on-demand when SKU consumption spikes). Events include the entitlement_id for reconciliation.

3) Proration: When an upgrade/downgrade happens, we emit a proration_delta event (type=proration) that specifies delta_units, effective_date, and prorated_amount. We also tag these events with invoice_period so AWS Marketplace can apply their billing rules.

4) Fallbacks & backfill: If runtime prefix/KV cache miss or write failure occurs, runtime writes a compact aggregate marker to a resilient queue (Kafka) and continues. A nightly backfill job replays raw events from the queue to S3 and attempts to reconstruct per-seat events when possible. If reconstruction is not possible within 72h, we emit an explicit aggregate_event with an "overflow=true" flag and attach a reconciliation_manifest for audit. See attached diagram for flow and a short note on idempotency keys.

SLA ask: we can commit to a 72-hour replay and reconciliation window; we’ll provide a reconciliation_manifest to AWS and Acme as part of the fulfillment webhook. Marcus — confirm final SLA before we put this in the listing doc.

Attachment: metering-fallback-diagram.png (PNG, 86KB)

From: alex.jenkins@amazon.com <aws_marketplace_pm@amazon.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Bcc:
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:36:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify bulk-license metering & proration for Acme Analytics SaaS listing

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Acme procurement confirms 72h replay SLA is acceptable for their contract provided we include a small credit term if reconciliation exceeds 72h (they asked for that as a safety).

Next steps: 
- Logan: please add the summarized bullets from Soojin into the listing documentation and attach the metering-fallback-diagram.png for AWS review.
- Redwood legal/procurement: we’ll include a brief clause in the listing that states: "Redwood will provide a reconciliation_manifest and backfill within 72 hours; if final reconciliation is delayed beyond 72 hours, Redwood will apply a 5% usage credit for the affected invoice period." Can you confirm acceptance?
- I’ll send a DocuSign outline for the listing addendum. Please review and sign by Fri 16 Apr so Acme can close the procurement window.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — please put the DocuSign link in this thread when ready.

Best,
Alex Jenkins
Product Manager, AWS Marketplace
Attachment: docusign-acme-listing.pdf (PDF, 24KB)
